- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to over-predict early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 2–3% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of downward trend), forecast should not continue downward beyond 2–3 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.7), model often over-optimistically forecasts upward trend — apply a 3–5% downward adjustment to the 10–15 day forecast window.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is consistently negative for 3+ days — otherwise, model tends to underestimate the depth of correction.
